Anthropic's valuation is everywhere, and most people get it wrong. Here's what it really means.
Anthropic makes Claude. In February, investors valued it at three hundred and eighty billion dollars.
By May, nine hundred and sixty-five billion. And this November, it listed on the stock market.
So what is a valuation? Think of Rohan's chai stall. It makes two laakh rupees a year.
A buyer offers him fifty laakh. Not for today's profit, but because he thinks it will become a chain.
Only if the chain never comes. A valuation is a bet on the future, not a price tag on today.
Investors are making the same bet. Anthropic's revenue grew fast, mostly from businesses paying for Claude.
The real story isn't the number. It's who's paying.
For you, it means businesses everywhere now pay for AI work. Your competitors are learning it too.
To be fair, bets can be wrong. Many dot-com giants were overvalued. And this isn't advice to buy any stock.
So skip the hype. Ask one question. What can AI do for my business this week?
Valuations are bets. Your time is real.
